target.name: Project Atlas (Healthcare Services target)
target.notes: Mid-market, private, regional, strong EBITDA margins

assumptions: Target region not specified: every named region scores as a footprint match; national / multi-regional deals score slightly lower.
'Strong EBITDA margin' taken as the dataset 75th percentile: 21.5%.
Implied target EBITDA ~$12.8M = $200M EV / anchor median 15.6x (illustrative, not given).
Recency measured from the latest year in the data (2024), not today's date.
Stated multiples are used as given and never recomputed.

rationale.headline: Platform-sized sponsor with 9 deals in 3 years, 4 prior Healthcare Services deals and zero withdrawals
rationale.acquirer_overview: Nordic Capital is a financial sponsor with 24 deals in 2016-2024, 9 of them in the last 3 years. Most deals are in Physician Groups (10) and Healthcare Services (4), with a size sweet spot of $35.0-302.1M (IQR). It most often buys from Private and PE-Backed sellers (9 each of 24), and its most common financing is All Cash (7 of 24). Its history shows a bias toward physician-led and dental assets, with a median target margin of 12.7% and median growth of 10.3%.
rationale.strategic_fit_thesis: Project Atlas is a platform for Nordic Capital: size_role is platform, inside its interquartile range $35.0-302.1M. Its own platform-labelled deals are smaller (3 deals, median $26.4M), and the dataset's deal_type labels are noisy, so we rely on the size band rather than the label. For example, [MA-2022-0103], a $222.1M Dental deal at 21.4% margin, is tagged Bolt-on Acquisition yet also carries Platform Build. The closest competitor is New Mountain Capital. The sharpest difference is sector depth: Nordic has 4 deals in Healthcare Services against 1 for New Mountain. Nordic also has 9 deals in the last 3 years against 5, and 0 withdrawn or terminated deals against 4. Nordic has 7 closed deals in the size band, 2 of them recent, so it can deploy at this size.

precedent_activity.why_relevant: Closest precedent: $222.1M Dental deal, 21.4% margin, 11.6x EV/EBITDA, closed 2022, usable as comp and close to the target's margin and size.
Most recent in-band-style deal: $76.0M Physician Groups recapitalization at 15.9x with 1 bidder, showing pace in 2024.
$301.0M Physician Groups recapitalization at 14.0x, top of its size range, closed with 2 bidders.
$388.8M leveraged buyout at 13.4x on a 7.4% margin target, shows willingness to go above the target's size.

rationale.valuation_context: Nordic's median of 13.8x across 6 comparable closed control deals (interquartile 13.4-14.7x) is in line with its Financial Sponsor peers at 13.5x, a 0.3 turn gap. Its highest-margin precedent, [MA-2022-0103] at 21.4%, cleared at 11.6x, while [MA-2024-0431] at a 16.8% margin went at 15.9x. Margin alone therefore does not set its price. Nordic's median target margin of 12.7% sits well below Atlas's 21.5%, so expect it to push on margin-adjusted value.

risk_flags.detail: Two stale pending or rumored deals, [MA-2020-0156] and [MA-2020-0291], with the largest withdrawn or pending at $232.9M, so announced intent has not always converted to closings.
Median target margin of 12.7% against Atlas's 21.5%; Nordic's high-margin precedent [MA-2022-0103] cleared at 11.6x, so its pricing may not reward margin.
Only 2 relevant closed deals out of 24 and 4 in the target sector; its largest closed deal of $1304.4M is far above Atlas, so sector evidence at this size is thin.

conviction.rationale: Held at the suggested High: 7 closed adjacent-sector deals in the size band, 2 in the last 3 years, 4 prior Healthcare Services deals, and no withdrawn deals. Thin relevance (2 relevant closed deals) is the main caveat.

+2 4 prior Healthcare Services deals

rationale.headline: Seven closed in-band deals and three Platform Investment deals make Atlas a platform-sized cheque for New Mountain.
rationale.acquirer_overview: New Mountain Capital is a financial sponsor with 21 deals in 2015-2024, 5 in the last 3 years; most deals are in Behavioral Health (5) and Physician Groups (5), its size sweet spot is $47.2-250.0M (IQR), it most often buys from Private sellers (13 of 21), and its most common financing is Earnout (6 of 21). Its history centers on services platforms, with only 1 Healthcare Services deal; deal-type labels such as Platform Investment (3) and Recapitalization (3) are noisy.
rationale.strategic_fit_thesis: Size role is platform, based on vs its 3 Platform Investment deals (median $314.8M), so a $200M Atlas would be a platform, not an add-on. Nearest platform precedents are [MA-2022-0377] at $228.4M and [MA-2022-0165] at $314.8M, both closed. [MA-2018-0470] is its one Healthcare Services deal, a $121.9M Leveraged Buyout with an 18.7% margin. On deployment pace, it has 5 deals in the last 3 years and 3 closed in-band deals in that window. Versus closest competitor Advent International, the difference is pricing: New Mountain's pricing position is below its peers while Advent's is in line with peers, on similar in-band depth (7 vs 6 closed). Tags such as Market Share and Cost Synergies are data points, not the thesis.

precedent_activity.why_relevant: Closed $228.4M Behavioral Health Platform Investment at 15.6x with a 17.4% margin; nearest size match and usable as a comp.
Its only Healthcare Services deal: $121.9M LBO at 12.3x, 18.7% margin, a single bidder, usable as a comp.
Closed $314.8M Platform Investment at 11.2x all cash, showing platform-sized cheques above the target size.
Closed $164.3M Revenue Cycle recapitalization at 15.3x with a 19.7% margin and 3 bidders, its highest-margin comp.

rationale.valuation_context: Across 6 closed adjacent-sector control deals in the size range, New Mountain's median is 11.8x EV/EBITDA (interquartile 9.7-14.6x) and 2.35x EV/revenue. Against Financial Sponsor peers at a 13.5x median, its pricing position is below its peers. Its range runs from 8.2x [MA-2022-0393] to 15.6x [MA-2022-0377], and the top of that range went to a 17.4% margin platform. A 21.5% margin seller may push it above its usual median.

risk_flags.detail: 4 of 21 deals were withdrawn or terminated, including [MA-2024-0216] in 2024 ($98.7M), and [MA-2020-0137] and [MA-2019-0119] are stale pending or rumored, so completion is not assured.
It prices below sponsor peers (11.8x vs 13.5x), and its median target margin is 15.9% against Atlas at 21.5%, so a price gap with the seller may arise.
Only 1 of 21 deals is in Healthcare Services [MA-2018-0470] and 2 relevant closed deals, so direct sector evidence is thin.

conviction.rationale: Staying at High: 7 closed deals in the size band, 3 of them in the last 3 years, and an 11.8x median inside the sponsor peer IQR of 11.5-15.6x. Tempered by 4 withdrawn or terminated deals.

rationale.headline: Blackstone has 6 closed deals in the size band and pays 1.1 turns above sponsor peers, but 2 withdrawals cap conviction.
rationale.acquirer_overview: Financial sponsor: 25 deals in 2015-2024, 6 in the last 3 years; most deals in Health Insurance (6) and Revenue Cycle (4); size sweet spot $70.7-595.7M (IQR); most often buys from Private sellers (9 of 25); most common financing is Stock (6 of 25). Its history is spread across 10 sectors, with Health Insurance and Revenue Cycle together making up 10 deals, so priorities lean toward those two rather than Healthcare Services, where it has 2 deals.
rationale.strategic_fit_thesis: As a sponsor, Blackstone would treat a $200M target as an add-on, not a platform: size_role is add-on, measured against its 4 Platform Investment deals (median $1102.8M). That means it would come via an existing portfolio company or platform. The target sits at the 32nd percentile of its deal sizes, and 6 closed deals fall in the size band, including Evergreen Care Solutions, a Healthcare Services bolt-on at $299.0M [MA-2021-0195]. Deployment pace is 6 deals in the last 3 years. Versus closest competitor Hellman & Friedman, Blackstone has 2 Healthcare Services deals against 0 and a median deal of $341.7M against $187.3M. Hellman & Friedman would see the target as a platform. Labels such as Bolt-on Acquisition (5) and Platform Investment (4) are noisy and are only supporting data points.

Dental management buyout at $222.5M, 13.5x, with a 20.1% margin close to the target's profile, and 4 bidders. Usable as comp.
Revenue Cycle bolt-on at $458.4M, 16.2x, 20.9% margin; the most recent in-band close for this buyer. Usable as comp.
Healthcare Services SPAC Merger at $341.7M, 10.0x; shows sector presence but is not usable as a control comp.

rationale.valuation_context: Blackstone's closed control comps (5 deals, adjacent sectors, similar size) show a median of 14.6x EV/EBITDA and 2.76x EV/revenue, with an interquartile range of 13.5x-16.2x. Against its Financial Sponsor peers (median 13.5x, n=54), its pricing is above, by 1.1 turns. Expect it to bid at the upper part of the sponsor range. The SPAC deal at 10.0x [MA-2021-0407] is excluded as a control comp.

Only 2 of 25 deals are in Healthcare Services and only 1 in-band deal closed in the last 3 years, so evidence for this exact sector and pace is thin.

conviction.rationale: Staying at the suggested Medium: 6 closed in-band deals and a 14.6x median inside the sponsor IQR support it, but only 1 recent in-band close and 2 withdrawals prevent an upgrade.

rationale.headline: Advent has closed 6 deals in the $67.3-312.1M band, 3 of them recently, so Project Atlas fits as a platform.
rationale.acquirer_overview: Advent International is a financial sponsor with 18 deals in 2016-2024, 5 of them in the last 3 years. Its most frequent sectors are Behavioral Health (3) and Revenue Cycle (3), and its size sweet spot is $67.3-312.1M (IQR). It most often buys from PE-Backed sellers (8 of 18), and All Cash is its most common financing (6 of 18). Its history spreads across 9 sectors, with Recapitalization (4) the most common deal type label, so it reads as a broad deployer rather than a single-sector specialist.
rationale.strategic_fit_thesis: Project Atlas at $200M is a platform for Advent, inside its interquartile range of $67.3-312.1M. Advent has 6 closed deals in the size band, 3 of them in the last 3 years, and its closed control comps in adjacent sectors include [MA-2024-0120] (Healthcare Services, $303.9M) and [MA-2023-0108] ($123.0M). Its 2 platform-labelled deals have a median of $29.6M, so the label is a weak guide and we lean on size and recency instead. The closest competitor is New Mountain Capital, which has 21 deals against Advent's 18 and 7 closed in the band against 6. The sharpest difference is pricing: Advent pays in line with its peers, while New Mountain pays below. That matters if the client wants a buyer that will not anchor low. Advent has only 1 prior Healthcare Services deal, so sector depth is thinner than its deployment pace.

precedent_activity.why_relevant: Closed 2024 Healthcare Services recapitalization at $303.9M and 9.3x EV/EBITDA, financed with stock; the same sector as Atlas and usable as a comp.
Closed 2023 Behavioral Health recapitalization at $123.0M and 14.6x, all cash, with a single bidder; shows recent in-band deployment.
Closed 2022 Revenue Cycle deal at $105.9M and 20.3x with a 21.8% margin, close to Atlas's margin profile; leveraged financing.

rationale.valuation_context: Advent's 4 closed control comps in adjacent sectors and in size range show a median of 13.4x EV/EBITDA (interquartile 11.6-16.0x) and 3.29x EV/revenue [MA-2024-0120][MA-2023-0108][MA-2022-0419]. Against Financial Sponsor peers, Advent pays in line with its peers (13.4x vs 13.5x, a gap of -0.1 turns). The highest multiple in its set, 20.3x, came with a 21.8% margin [MA-2022-0419]. The lowest, 9.3x, came from a 13.9% margin non-profit seller [MA-2024-0120]. Margin therefore appears to drive its price spread.

risk_flags.detail: Advent has 3 withdrawn or terminated deals out of 18: [MA-2018-0206], [MA-2019-0418] and [MA-2024-0042]. The last, a $1,114.0M deal in 2024, is recent.
Its median target margin is 14.5% against Atlas's 21.5%, and its in-set multiples range from 9.3x to 20.3x. Pricing a high-margin asset may need a stretch from its usual spread.
Only 1 of its 18 deals is in Healthcare Services [MA-2024-0120], and its deals span 9 sectors, so sector-specific platform depth is limited.

conviction.rationale: Staying at High: 6 closed in-band deals, 3 in the last 3 years, and a 13.4x median inside the peer IQR of 11.5-15.6x. Tempered by 3 withdrawn or terminated deals and only 1 Healthcare Services deal.

rationale.strategic_fit_thesis: The size role is platform, inside its interquartile range $88.6-437.2M, so Project Atlas at $200M would be a standalone platform rather than an add-on. Nearest adjacent evidence is physician and billing services: [MA-2024-0002] at $298.6M, 5 bidders, and [MA-2023-0379] at $446.8M in Revenue Cycle with a 24.2% margin, close to Atlas's 21.5%. Deployment pace is lower, 5 deals in the last 3 years vs 8. H&F's median size sits close to Atlas's $200M, but it has less pace and no sector history.

33.3% of deals are leveraged or seller-financed, and 3 deals are stock-financed. A $200M platform sits well below its largest closed deal of $994.1M, so size is not the constraint.
